asof: Settles Thu 29 Oct 2026 · written Fri 30 Oct
headline: SR3 extends the post-Fed rally, 2027 down 11–13bp; U7 peak 4.515% now about one hike above the Fed's dots.
summary: The strip rallied hard for a second day, led by U7 and Z7, which fell 13bp in implied rate, with M7 down 11.5bp, H7 8bp and Z6 4.5bp while U6 was unchanged at 3.923%; the 2028–29 contracts fell 8–12.5bp. That turns the week into a rally: M7 is 9bp and U7 9.5bp lower since Friday. Month to date Z6 is 15.5bp and Z7 37.7bp lower than the end-September (modelled) settles. The peak is still SR3U7, now at 4.515%, 57.5bp over the latest 3.94% SOFR fixing with only 8bp of easing priced from there to Z9, against a Fed median that sees one more hike to 4.125%.
drivers: Data good enough for December, not for 2027

Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualised against 3.1% expected and claims fell to 194,000, but September core PCE was in line at 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y, quarterly core PCE slowed to 2.5% from 3.3%, and income (0.2%) and spending (0.5%) both missed. The market kept December but trimmed what follows: M7 to Z7 fell 11.5–13bp in rate and the 2-year yield settled 3.1bp lower at 4.654%.
Global hikes now come with a pause

The ECB held and all but promised a December hike, but sources said it expects to pause after that because higher bond yields are already weighing on growth, which pulled Bund and Treasury yields lower together. Read across, the strip took out part of the 2027 tightening behind the December hike, so Z6/M7 narrowed 7bp to +32.5bp.
Risk-off on AI spending, solid supply

Alphabet fell about 13% after a revenue miss and heavier AI cash burn, and the Nasdaq lost 1.4%, adding a growth scare to the bid for the 2027–28 contracts. The $44bn 7-year cleared at 4.894%, on the when-issued level, with the dealer take down to 9.4%, so supply did not stand in the way.

Brent settled 44 cents lower at $114.88 and WTI 78 cents lower at $102.00 as the US floated a temporary peace proposal to Iran through Qatar, though it is still up more than 17% this month. SOFR printed 3.94% for 28 October, 6bp over EFFR, and U6 did not move ahead of the 30 October month-end.
spreads: The whites flattened sharply as the 2027 hikes came out: U6/Z6 narrowed 4.5bp to +22.2bp (−10.1bp month to date), Z6/H7 3.5bp to +20bp (−11.6bp) and H7/M7 3.5bp to +12.5bp (−6.3bp), while M7/U7 narrowed 1.5bp to +4.5bp and U7/Z7 held at −1.5bp, so the peak stays in U7 with almost nothing priced in Z7. Z6/Z7 fell 8.5bp to +35.5bp, 6.5bp narrower on the week and 22.2bp narrower than at end-September. The reds and greens steepened again: Z7/Z8 +3bp to −4bp (+4bp on the week), U7/Z8 +3bp to −5.5bp and Z8/Z9 +2bp to −2.5bp, with every quarterly spread from Z7/H8 out a touch less inverted; there is no month-to-date base before 20 October for these. Flies cheapened slightly: H7/M7/U7 fell 2bp to +8bp (−3.8bp month to date) and M7/U7/Z7 1.5bp to +6bp.
fed: Fed funds futures were last recorded at Wednesday's post-FOMC close: 21.8bp for the 9 December meeting (an 87% chance of a hike), 31bp by January, 46.5bp by March, 65bp by June and a 73.5bp peak at the October 2027 FOMC (implied EFFR 4.615%). That compares with 22.6bp, 49.1bp and a 76.5bp peak the day before, 26.5bp, 56.8bp and 85bp a week earlier, and 30.6bp, 63.4bp and a 94bp peak at end-September; Newsquawk put December near 20bp on Thursday. SR3 has gone further: U7 at 4.515% sits 10bp below that ZQ peak even though SOFR is fixing 6bp over EFFR, so Thursday's rally took roughly another 15bp of 2027 hikes out that ZQ has yet to record. The strip now implies about 57bp of tightening to the peak, against a Reuters poll in which all 100 economists expect a December hike and a September median dot of 4.125% held through 2027, so the market still prices roughly one hike more than the Fed.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 5.5bp in favour at +32.5bp after narrowing 7bp on Thursday; it is 17.9bp narrower than at end-September and 12.5bp from target. The trade is working as planned, with Z6 holding the December hike (Z6 fell only 4.5bp) while M7 shed 11.5bp of later tightening. Stop trailed to +40bp to keep reward at about 1.7 times risk from here.
ideas.risk: A firm ECI on Friday or a strong October payrolls report would revive the second 2027 hike and push the spread back toward +40bp.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open and 4bp against at −4bp: Z7 rallied 13bp in price on Thursday against 10bp for Z8, so the hedge gave back 3bp while the core gained 7bp, the trade-off it is meant to provide. Only 6.5bp of easing is priced from Z7 to Z9, little if a Fed that has already hiked once with Brent near $115 has to unwind. Keep at about half the core size; stop +2bp is 6bp away, target −25bp.
ideas.risk: If the market keeps pricing out 2027 hikes the reds can flatten toward zero and push the spread through the stop.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 was unchanged at 3.923% implied while the rest of the strip rallied 4.5–13bp, because its remaining exposure is mostly realised fixings: SOFR printed 3.94% for 28 October, above that average. The 30 October month-end and the 3 November bill settlement could keep fixings firm, and only the final week of U6 sees the December decision; revisit after the month-end prints.
ideas.risk: A soft month-end with SOFR back near 3.88% would leave a few bp of upside on the table.

watch: Q3 employment cost index, Chicago PMI, month-end
ECI is seen at 0.8% after 0.9%; a firm print would test the 2027 rally, and month-end shows whether SOFR holds near 3.94%.
Prices paid was 77.9 in September; the estimate updates the $628bn Q4 borrowing figure and bill supply.
Fiscal outlook and term premium for the reds and greens; Gulf strike risk is reported for after the vote.
Coupon sizes and the bill share drive term premium in the reds; services prices matter for the 2027 hikes.
September added only 29,000; a soft report would extend the 2027 rally, a firm one would revive it.
Brent at $114.88 is the main risk to fading 2027 hikes; a peace deal would add to the rally.
